title: Orthogonality of product monomials
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be mutually independent real random variables in $L^2$, each with mean zero and second moment one. For subsets $S,T\subseteq I$, $\mathbb E\big[(\prod_{i\in S}X_i)(\prod_{i\in T}X_i)\big]$ equals $1$ if $S=T$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: the random variables are mutually independent
each random variable has mean zero
each random variable has second moment one
replaced: Let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, with $I$ finite, $X_i\in L^2$, $\E X_i=0$, and $\E X_i^2=1$ for every $i$. For $S,T\subseteq I$, $\E[(\prod_{i\in S}X_i)(\prod_{i\in T}X_i)]=1$ if $S=T$, and $0$ otherwise.
